concepts.name: Threshold of the First Cup
concepts.big_idea: The grand opening is staged as a doorway built from the warung counter itself, so the first cup passes through the shop rather than sitting in front of it.
concepts.creative_tension: A new business must feel established on its first day, so permanence is borrowed from the counter while the cup remains a first arrival.
concepts.visual_metaphor: The serving counter is framed as an architectural threshold, its edge acting as a lintel above the waiting cup.
concepts.why: A launch needs recognition before appetite; showing the shop as a place already standing tells passersby the counter will be there tomorrow.
concepts.visual_world: Early morning inside a narrow Solo storefront, teak counter edge, condensation on steel, daylight arriving from the street side.
concepts.risk: Reads as quiet and may lose against louder promotional posts in a scroll.

concepts.name: Queue as the Announcement
concepts.big_idea: The opening is told through the students who arrive first, their waiting bodies forming the headline the shop cannot yet claim for itself.
concepts.creative_tension: A shop nobody knows must borrow credibility from the people willing to stand in it.
concepts.visual_metaphor: A line of young customers curves along the counter, their posture spelling the shape of the word opening.
concepts.why: Young buyers trust peers over claims; showing the crowd converts the launch into social proof rather than an assertion.
concepts.visual_world: Street kerb outside the shop at mid morning, uniform bags, motorbike helmets held in hands, tiled pavement.
concepts.risk: Requires real people on the day and cannot be shot before opening.

concepts.name: Measured Pour
concepts.big_idea: One uninterrupted pour is held in a tall column of empty space, reducing the whole opening to a single unhurried gesture.
concepts.creative_tension: A launch shouts, but the product is made by patience, so the gesture must slow the surface down.
concepts.visual_metaphor: A thin stream of coffee descends through a vertical void, meeting the cup near the lower edge.
concepts.why: Restraint separates the shop from promotional noise and states that quality precedes volume.
concepts.visual_world: Bare plaster wall, single steel kettle, narrow table, morning shade with no props.
concepts.risk: Quiet enough that the opening date must carry weight in the layout.
